new_statements.quote: However, positing Proto-Philippine forms allows for reconstructions with contrastive stress, which is retained in many Philippine languages (including Tagalog, Standard Bikol, and Manide) but has not been reliably reconstructed to PMP. [fn. 16] ... Lawrence Reid (pers. comm., June 26, 2010) points out that the stress assignment in the Manide form points to a source in PMP *zuRuq with Back Vowel Fronting. ... new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Manide has an empty rule. Lobel's footnote supplies a type (contrastive/lexical stress retained, as in Tagalog and Standard Bikol) but not a placement rule, so it refines the empty record rather than agreeing or contradicting. This work was not in the listed 'works' for this task (it was downloaded 2026-09-16 and is held by the project); it is reported here because it is the only opened text with a stress statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lobel states only that Manide retains the contrastive (lexically distinctive) stress of the Philippine type, i.e. stress placement is a lexical property of the word (penult vs. ultima in the Philippine pattern) rather than fixed; he gives no rule for placement, no domain statement and no description of secondary stress. The section-2 phonology discussion covers segmental reflexes only; there is no suprasegmentals subsection, and the phoneme inventory (table 2) is not reproduced in the Gale text.
new_statements.exceptions: fn. 18: some forms do not reflect the reconstructed (Proto-Philippine) stress; digi 'blood' has a stress assignment that Reid reads as pointing to PMP *zuRuq rather than *daRaq.
new_statements.identity_note: Lobel 2010 describes Manide of Camarines Norte (Negrito language, Manide-Alabat group); his data also cover the closely related Inagta Alabat, but the stress remarks in fns. 16 and 18 name Manide specifically. Doroja 2017 (unopened) is, by its title, a sketch of Manide proper.
